subject.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto

question: Should a critical tool-loop veto terminate every supported runtime, and must pending steering or follow-up input survive for the next run rather than being discarded?
rationale: The issue defines a global safety outcome, but runtime ownership and queued-input semantics differ across embedded agent-core, Codex, and other harnesses; the contributor cannot safely choose that product boundary alone.

options.title: Complete cross-runtime termination
options.body: Wire each harness to its native stop mechanism and preserve or requeue pending user input before merging one canonical PR.

options.title: Scope to embedded runtime
options.body: Limit the promise and implementation to the embedded AgentSession path, document that limitation, and track external harness termination separately.

options.title: Accept immediate message loss
options.body: Merge the embedded stop with an explicit owner decision that critical vetoes may discard queued steering and follow-up messages.

recommendation.title: Complete cross-runtime termination
recommendation.body: Wire each harness to its native stop mechanism and preserve or requeue pending user input before merging one canonical PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent-runtime history makes this person the best available owner for the cross-runtime and pending-message decision.
